Thanks again for the call this morning — great to meet the team and walk through LegacyBank's on-prem, air-gapped requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned:

- Fully offline deployment (air-gapped) inside LegacyBank data centers
- Hardware owned/managed by LegacyBank, with software delivered via signed packages or physical media

2) Network topology — we need a high-level diagram of the airgap boundary and management jump hosts (attached a template).
3) Maintenance policy — confirm allowed weekly maintenance window and whether we can schedule quarterly software updates requiring physical media access.

Proposed next steps:
- I will send our up-to-date hardware requirements and an airgap checklist (attached). Please fill the checklist and return prior to the technical workshop.
- Dev will join a 90-minute technical workshop next week to run through install/upgrade flow, offline package process, and logging/monitoring expectations. Suggested dates: May 25 or May 27 (please confirm).
- We will prepare a draft Dedicated/Private proposal and a scoped quote for procurement once we confirm hardware SKUs and timeline.

Attachments included: redwood_onprem_hardware_requirements_v2.pdf, network_topology_drawing.png, legacybank_airgap_checklist.xlsx

Alex / Priya — adding a few technical clarifications from the infra side: 

1) Supported GPU SKUs & recommended config:
- Supported: NVIDIA A10, A30, A100 (we support mixed clusters).
- Recommendation for production inference at scale: A100 (40GB) with 512GB system RAM per host, NVMe for model cache. If you want lower-cost scale-out for non-critical workloads, A30 is fine but expect higher latency for large context.

2) Offline upgrade path (air-gapped):
- Primary delivery options we support: signed artifact bundles (tgz) that you can transfer via secure USB or internal artifact repo. Bundles include package signatures (PKCS7) and checksums.
- For chain-of-custody we support a two-person verification step during install; we can provide an installer checklist that your on-site engineer signs off.
- If you require physical media handling, we also provide a validated USB image option with an HMAC-signed manifest.

3) High-availability and upgrades:
- Rolling upgrade supported with offline workers staged in maintenance window; for fully isolated racks you can leverage a blue/green approach where we provision a parallel set, validate offline, and switch traffic during maintenance window.

4) Logs & audit:
- Runtime writes to local encrypted logs; we can export signed audit bundles post-maintenance for your retention. KMS integration will be customer-managed and we provide the plugin to talk to the vault endpoint over the management network.

Attachments: small install script stubs and the offline upgrade checklist (attached to thread by Marissa).

We'll confirm the package signing format and provide a sample signed bundle prior to the workshop.

Thanks — Dev
